definitions.explanation: A writer of exceptional talent and lasting influence. Used to describe authors whose works have become part of the literary canon.

examples.japanese: {夏目|なつめ}{漱石|そうせき}は{日本|にほん}の{文豪|ぶんごう}だ。
examples.english: Natsume Soseki is a great Japanese author.

examples.japanese: {文豪|ぶんごう}たちが{愛|あい}した{旅館|りょかん}を{訪|たず}ねた。
examples.english: I visited the inn that was loved by the literary masters.

examples.japanese: この{町|まち}には{明治|めいじ}{時代|じだい}の{文豪|ぶんごう}ゆかりの{地|ち}が{数多|かずおお}く{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: In this town, many sites associated with Meiji-era literary masters still remain.

notes:
USAGE:
A respectful title used for established, canonical writers. In Japan, often applied to Meiji- and Taisho-era novelists such as {夏目|なつめ}{漱石|そうせき}, {太宰|だざい}{治|おさむ}, {芥川|あくたがわ}{龍之介|りゅうのすけ}, and {森|もり}{鷗外|おうがい}. Not typically used for living authors.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {日本|にほん}の{文豪|ぶんごう}: great Japanese author
- {文豪|ぶんごう}の{作品|さくひん}: works of a literary master
- {文豪|ぶんごう}ゆかりの{地|ち}: places associated with a literary master

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {作家|さっか}: writer, author (general, neutral)
- {小説家|しょうせつか}: novelist (neutral)
